page: Amazon Web Services x8g.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and AWS Neoverse-V2 arm64 architecture. The server provides 2 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial relative to compute, delivering 32.0 GB of system RAM, which yields an allocation ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions are present, while vector and matrix extensions such as AVX or AMX are absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable single-threaded execution balanced against limited aggregate compute throughput. In stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, single-core scores fall within the middle 50% range, whereas multi-core compute tests register in the lower 25% bracket due to the two-core ceiling. Memory bandwidth benchmarks yield 53.78 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 21.69 GB/sec on large-block writes. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs in the top 25% at 14.38 GB/sec, while database operations and PassMark memory metrics align with average cloud baselines. In-memory data store workloads recorded 4.65 million Redis SET operations per second.

The instance relies exclusively on network-attached storage, as zero local NVMe storage is bundled. Network bandwidth is provisioned at a 1 Gbps baseline, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. From a cost efficiency perspective, x8g.large targets applications with disproportionately high memory demands relative to compute, avoiding the need to overprovision unnecessary CPU cores. This hardware profile is most fitting for lightweight in-memory caching layers, medium-scale Redis deployments, key-value data stores, and memory-constrained backend services.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.large is a memory-optimized instance driven by 2 dedicated arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an elevated memory density of 16.0 GB per vCPU alongside 36 MB of L3 cache. Benchmark assessments reflect solid single-thread performance, including top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory write bandwidth are constrained by the two-core limit. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and offers a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. With dedicated hardware threads and AES acceleration, x8g.large provides a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive setups that do not warrant high core counts. Workload fit includes in-memory key-value databases, Redis caching layers, text processing, and auxiliary microservices requiring substantial memory footprints.
